options: The members of Election Commission do not have equal powers with Chief Election Commissioner
Disputes related to the Election are not decided by the Election Commission only
The Election Commission of India enjoys Constitutional status
Keeping the voters list updated at all times is the responsibility of Elections Commission
key_text: The members of Election Commission do not have equal powers with Chief Election Commissioner
explanation: The CEC and the ECs have equal powers and equal salaries, so statement (1) is the incorrect one. Election disputes go to the courts, the ECI is a constitutional body, and it keeps electoral rolls updated.

notes.text: - All members have **equal powers**; decisions by **majority** – upheld in **T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995)**.

q:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true relating to Election Commission of India?

A. The Election Commission of India is a three member Body.

B. The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India.

C. Election Commission of India is a Constitutional Body.
explanation: A and C are true: the ECI is a three-member body (CEC + 2 ECs) and a constitutional body under Art. 324. B is false – the President, not the CJI, appoints the CEC.

notes.text: - **CEC + such number of ECs as the President fixes**; today **CEC + 2 ECs = a three-member body** (APPSC G2 2025 – "three member body" and "constitutional body" are true; "appointed by the CJI" is false).

q: Election Commission of India derives its power from which article of the constitution of India?
explanation: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission; Arts 321-323 concern Public Service Commissions and 344 the Official Language Commission.

notes.text: - A **permanent, independent constitutional body** set up directly by the Constitution – **Part XV ("Elections"), Articles 324-329**; basis **Art. 324**; an **all-India body common to the Centre and the States**.

q: Who allots election symbols to political parties in India?
explanation: The Election Commission recognises parties and allots election symbols under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968; the Speaker, PM and President have no role.

notes.text: - **Recognises parties and allots symbols** (**Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968**) and acts as a court on **splits/mergers and symbol disputes** – not the Speaker, PM or President.

q:
The powers of the Election Commission include which of the following ?

I. The Election Commission takes decisions on every aspect of conduct and control of elections from the announcement of elections to the declaration of results.

II. During the election period, the Election Commission can order the Government to dismiss some government officials.

III. When on election duty, Government officers work under the control of the Election Commission.
explanation: I and III are correct (NCERT): the ECI decides every aspect from announcement to results, and officers on election duty work under its control. II is wrong – it can issue guidelines and order transfers, not dismissal of officials.

notes.text: - Superintendence, direction and control of **electoral rolls** and **conduct of elections** to **Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President** (Art. 324(1)); decides **every aspect from the announcement of elections to the declaration of results** (APPSC G1 2023).

- **Officers on election duty work under the ECI's control**, not the government's; staff preparing rolls are deemed on **deputation** to the ECI. It can issue guidelines and order **transfers/suspension** – it does **not** order the government to **dismiss** officials.

q: In case a member of the Lok Sabha becomes liable for disqualification (for reasons other than defection), whose decision would be final?
options: Speaker after consultation with Election Commission of India
President after consultation with Election Commission of India
key_text: President after consultation with Election Commission of India
explanation: For disqualifications other than defection the President's decision is final under Art. 103, taken after obtaining – and acting on – the Election Commission's opinion; defection cases go to the Speaker.

notes.text: - Advises the **President on MPs' disqualification (Art. 103)** – the **President decides after obtaining the ECI's opinion and acts on it** – and the **Governor on MLAs' (Art. 192)**.

q:
In the context of the Indian Constitution, which of the following statements is/are true?

A. The Election Commission of India administers elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, Panchayats, Municipalities, the President and Vice-President of India.

B. Part-XVIII of the Constitution deals with the emergency powers of the President.

C. The kind of transformation of the political system from federal (during normal times) to unitary (during emergency) is a borrowed feature from the Weimar Constitution.
explanation: Only B: Part XVIII (Arts 352-360) contains the emergency provisions. A is false – Panchayat and municipal polls are under the State Election Commissions. C is false – the federal-to-unitary transformation in an Emergency is a unique feature of the Constitution; Weimar gave only the suspension of FRs.

notes.text: - So "the ECI administers elections to Panchayats and Municipalities" is **false**; co-operative societies and banks are not SEC elections either.

- Other facts for app MCQs: emergency provisions are **Part XVIII**; the federal-to-unitary switch in an Emergency is a **unique feature** of the Constitution (Laxmikanth), **not** borrowed from Weimar (Weimar = suspension of FRs).
